why: p0001 scores 0.666667 with a constant array.
statement: The constant step function with 50 equal heights has R = 2/3 exactly.

why: Direct computation of the piecewise-linear convolution formula gives 196/288.
statement: A symmetric peaked step shape such as h=[1,2,1] exceeds the constant value: exact evaluation gives R≈0.68056.
refuted_if: An exact run of [1,2,1] or its scaled/padded version scores at or below 2/3.

why: The [1,2,1] calculation suggests this mechanism.
statement: Peaked unimodal h makes f*f less triangular and relatively fuller near its maximum, increasing ||f*f||_2^2 relative to ||f*f||_inf while keeping ||f*f||_1 fixed.
refuted_if: Optimization finds that flat or U-shaped h systematically beats all peaked unimodal shapes.

why: Smooth bumps already beat constant; isolated spikes appear penalized by the 2/3 knot factor.
statement: The best shapes are symmetric unimodal bumps; sparse multi-spike or highly asymmetric shapes score below the best smooth bump.
refuted_if: A sparse or asymmetric construction scores higher than the best unimodal bump found.

why: Three independent constructions all beat 2/3 by large margins.
statement: Peaked non-flat shapes substantially exceed 2/3: free-form optimized bumps reach 0.72-0.84, versus 2/3 for the constant.

why: The best shapes are peaked bumps, not flat; consistent with the mechanism.
statement: A peaked (non-flat) f makes f*f fuller near its maximum relative to ||f*f||_inf, raising R while ||f*f||_1 is fixed by scaling.

why: p0003 is clearly asymmetric yet is the best found, contradicting the old 'symmetric' claim.
statement: The best shape is an asymmetric dense bump with a few zero steps (p0003 peak at 0.65 of support, ~12% zeros), not a symmetric unimodal profile.

why: Suggests resolution, not just basin, is a lever.
statement: Higher step resolution improves R: N=50 (0.8404) beats N=21 (0.8289), so refining the best shape to N>=100 can exceed 0.85.
refuted_if: Multiscale refinement of p0003 at N=100-200 fails to beat 0.8404.

why: Both winning shapes are dense bumps; worth testing directly.
statement: The optimum is a single dense asymmetric bump, not a sparse multi-spike comb or difference-set construction.
refuted_if: A comb/difference-set or strongly multi-hump construction scores above the best dense bump.

why: p0013's autoconvolution peak at center is a hint of symmetry, contradicting the earlier asymmetric reading.
statement: The best shape is a dense bump with a few zero steps; whether it is asymmetric is now unclear: early best p0003 peaked at 0.65 of support, but current best p0013 has its f*f maximum at 0.500 of support, suggesting a near-symmetric profile.

why: p0010's stage lines show no gain at N=100/200, while p0013 at N=100 reached 0.841166; gains are tiny.
statement: Higher resolution gives only small gains: N=50 -> 0.8409, N=100 -> 0.8412, and p0010's upsampling to N=200 gave no further gain. Resolution is near-saturated; N>=100 will not reach 0.85.

why: Both structural and sparse-basin experiments underperform the dense bump.
statement: The optimum is a single dense bump, not a sparse multi-spike comb: p0011's structural moves from p0003 found nothing and p0012's sparse p0005 basin refined only to 0.8278.

why: Diminishing returns across independent 30 s runs indicate the local-search mechanism is exhausted.
statement: Random-mutation local/memetic search saturates near 0.841: the last three 30 s runs gained at most ~0.0008 each (p0010 +0.00045, p0011 +0.000004, p0013 +0.00076).

why: p0019's pgd200/pgd400 stages gained 0 and p0017 gained 5e-6, while perturb-restart stages gained ~1e-3.
statement: Plain local ascent (random mutation, numerical-gradient Adam, golden-section coordinate ascent) saturates near 0.841; real gains come only from perturb-then-reoptimize restart cycles (p0019 polish +0.0013, p0015 perturb +0.0010).

why: Explains why both gradient and coordinate ascent stalled while random perturb restarts worked.
statement: The hard max in ||f*f||_inf makes the numerical gradient sparse/noisy (only the argmax knot contributes to the denominator), so smooth ascent stalls; replacing max by a soft-max (log-sum-exp, annealed temperature) should give dense gradients and faster ascent.
refuted_if: Softmax-smoothed gradient ascent at N=200 gains less than 1e-4 over 20+ s while perturb-restart cycles on the same base gain more.

why: p0016 symmetrized and reoptimized to exactly 0.841166; p0019's max sits at 0.355.
statement: Symmetry is not a disadvantage: symmetric-constrained optimization matches the asymmetric 0.841166 exactly. Yet the current best (p0019, 0.842478) has its f*f maximum at 0.355 of support, so mild asymmetry appears at the top.

why: p0019's best stayed at N=100; p0015's gain came after upsampling to 3200 plus perturb restarts.
statement: Resolution alone gives little (p0019 kept N=100 and still improved); resolution only pays when combined with perturb-restart cycles (p0015 at N=3200, +0.0010).

text: Best is a dense peaked bump; constant gives 2/3. Free-form hard-max optimization reaches about 0.84, but softmax smoothing of ||f*f||_inf is the big lever, lifting p0023 to 0.873353. Perturb-restart cycles still help, yet softmax gradients matter more. Resolution alone gives little; the high-resolution branch lags. Open questions: optimal softmax temperature/annealing, whether high-resolution softmax closes the gap, and whether sparse or multi-hump constructions can challenge the single dense bump.

why: p0025 is the strongest hard-max attempt so far and still lags the softmax line by 0.030.
statement: Hard-max local ascent saturates near 0.844 even with analytic gradients and high-resolution stages (p0025 0.843737, +0.00126 over p0019), while softmax-smoothed ascent gains an order of magnitude more (p0023 0.8425->0.8734).

why: Two independent lines now separate smoothing from optimizer quality.
statement: The hard max makes gradients sparse (only the argmax knot contributes); replacing it with softmax_T (log-sum-exp, annealed T) gives dense gradients weighting all near-max knots and is the main lever found so far. p0025's fast analytic hard-max gradient reaching only 0.8437 supports this: speed without smoothing does not help.

why: Shape statistics of the record construction.
statement: The best construction (p0023) has a peaked f (max/mean = 5.0) but a flat-topped, asymmetric f*f: 39% of knots within 5% of the maximum, max at 0.307 of support, ||f*f||_inf = 0.893.
refuted_if: a construction that does better than this statement says is possible

why: p0023's f*f plateau is the clearest structural difference from the 0.84 family.
statement: R is driven by making f*f as flat as possible over as wide a region as possible while keeping its sup low; constructions whose f*f is sharply peaked should not beat the flat-topped best.
refuted_if: A construction whose f*f has fewer than 10% of knots within 5% of its maximum scores above 0.873353.

why: p0023 spent ~400 convolutions per gradient; p0025 shows the analytic trick works.
statement: Replacing p0023's finite-difference softmax gradients with analytic ones (plus higher N) will gain at least 1e-3 over 0.873353 within one 30 s run.
refuted_if: An analytic-gradient softmax run with >=25 s of ascent gains less than 1e-4 over 0.873353.

why: Best now 0.9045, well beyond the earlier 0.72-0.84 range.
statement: Peaked non-flat shapes vastly exceed 2/3: free-form optimized bumps climb from 0.72 to 0.90 as the optimizer improves (p0003 0.840, p0023 0.873, p0030 0.9045).

why: Stage lines show diminishing returns from pure higher N; multi-scale re-opt did better.
statement: Resolution alone gives little: p0030's N=400/800 stages added only +0.0022/+0.001 after N=200. Multi-scale continuation with per-scale re-optimization pays more (p0031 +0.0117).

why: Explore result 0.8353 < 0.84 threshold, negative structural result.
statement: The optimum is a single dense bump, not sparse/comb: p0029's sparse/comb/multi-hump search from scratch reached only 0.8353, far below the dense 0.9045.

why: p0030 confirms analytic softmax is the big lever.
statement: Hard-max local ascent saturates ~0.844, while analytic-gradient softmax ascent is the dominant lever: p0030 gained +0.031 over p0023. Gradient speed alone (p0025) is not enough.

why: Direct evidence from p0030.
statement: Replacing the hard max with softmax_T (log-sum-exp, annealed T) gives dense gradients weighting all near-max knots and is the main lever found: analytic softmax lifted p0023 0.8734->0.9045.

why: Updated stats from the new best.
statement: The best construction (p0030) is a peaked f (max/mean 11.5, 39.6% zeros) with a flat-topped asymmetric f*f: 41.66% of knots within 5% of max, max at 0.383 of support, ||f*f||_inf=0.8719.

why: New best has a wider near-max plateau than p0023.
statement: R is driven by making f*f flat over a wide region while keeping its sup low; p0030's f*f has 41.66% of knots within 5% of max and max at 0.383 of support.

why: Prediction held decisively.
statement: Analytic softmax gradients with higher N gained +0.031 over 0.873353 in one run (p0030), confirming the prediction by a wide margin.

why: p0030's perturb (7 restarts) and polish stages gave 0.904528->0.904529.
statement: The current p0030 basin is locally saturated: perturb restarts and hard-R coordinate polish after softmax add < 1e-5, so further gains require escaping the basin (re-heating or coarsening), not more polishing.
refuted_if: A run that only polishes/restarts p0030 (no re-heating, no coarsening) gains > 1e-3.

why: The challenge experiment p0037 was designed exactly to break B5 and confirmed it.
statement: Resolution alone gives little: pure N=3200 softmax ascent from p0030 gained exactly 0.000000 (p0037). Gains come from escaping the basin at fixed N by re-heating (+0.00263, p0034) or by coarsening then re-ascending (+0.00122, p0036).

why: Independent line p0035 reproduces the big analytic-softmax gain.
statement: Hard-max local ascent saturates ~0.844; analytic-gradient softmax ascent is the dominant lever (p0030 +0.031, p0035 +0.0398 in the mutation loop, p0034 +0.0026 on top of it). Gradient speed alone is not enough.

why: Re-heating, the T-schedule extension of this mechanism, produced the new best.
statement: Replacing the hard max with softmax_T (log-sum-exp, annealed T) gives dense gradients weighting all near-max knots and is the main lever found; re-heating T back to ~1e-3*maxL after annealing to 1e-6*maxL escapes the local basin.

why: Both escape mechanisms gained; p0034's own polish stage added 0.000000.
statement: The p0030/p0034 basin is locally saturated: pure polishing/restarts add <1e-5, but re-heating (+0.00263, p0034) and coarsening (+0.00122, p0036) both escape it. Escape, not polish, is where the remaining gains are.

why: Updated to the new best's measured statistics.
statement: The best construction (p0034) is a peaked f (max/mean 11.97, 40.8% zeros) with a flat-topped asymmetric f*f: 41.79% of knots within 5% of max, max at 0.522 of support, ||f*f||_inf=0.8704. The f*f max location has drifted from 0.383 (p0030) to 0.522, i.e. the best shapes are getting more asymmetric.

why: Plateau statistics of the new best.
statement: R is driven by making f*f flat over a wide region while keeping its sup low; p0034's f*f has 41.79% of knots within 5% of max (28.98% within 0.1%) with max at 0.522 of support.

why: It was a one-off prediction about p0030 that has been confirmed and is now subsumed by B7/B8.
Subsumed by B9/B10; keeping it adds no decision value.
Only one cycle fit in p0034's budget yet it delivered the round's biggest gain.
statement: Temperature re-heating at fixed N is a cheap escape: one cycle (multiplicative perturb sigma 0.01-0.03, re-anneal T from 1e-3 to 1e-6*maxL) gained +0.00263 on p0030 in only 7.5 s, so spending nearly the whole budget on many such cycles should pay more than one.
refuted_if: A run from p0034 with 8+ reheat cycles at N=800 (no low-N stages) gains less than 1e-4.

why: Two independent runs show coarsening moves the solution, unlike pure high-N ascent.
statement: Coarsening to N=400 and re-ascending reaches regions the N=800 ascent cannot: p0034's soft400 stage gained +0.0022 and p0036's coarsen+re-ascend gained +0.0012, both more than pure N=800 polishing.
refuted_if: A coarsen-to-400 + reheat ladder from p0034 (400 -> 800 -> 1600) gains less than 1e-4.

why: Both reheat and ladder gave only ~4e-4, so the mechanism works but is near saturation.
statement: Re-heating at fixed N is a cheap escape but saturates: p0043's 4 cycles at N=800 gained +0.000411 (0.907159->0.907570), and p0042's 400->800->1600 ladder gained +0.000400; gains are now ~4e-4, not 1e-3.

why: p0043 and p0040 show polishing/restarts add little.
statement: The p0043 basin is nearly saturated: many reheat cycles at N=800 gained only +0.000411, and exact hard-R polish after softmax anneal added only +0.000004 (p0040). Remaining gains are small escapes (~1e-4-5e-4), not large.

why: Updated stats and noted max-location variability.
statement: The best construction p0043 is a peaked f (max/mean 13.14, 41.1% zeros) with a flat-topped asymmetric f*f: 41.79% of knots within 5% of max, 28.29% within 0.1%, max at 0.302 of support, ||f*f||_inf=0.871268. The f*f max location is not stable across high scorers (0.302 p0043, 0.373 p0042, 0.524 p0040), so it is not a reliable design target.

why: New best supports the flat-plateau picture.
statement: R is driven by making f*f flat over a wide region while keeping sup low: p0043 has 41.79% of knots within 5% of max (28.29% within 0.1%) and scores 0.907570; p0040 with 41.46% within 5% scores 0.904962.

why: Rules out hard polish as a useful final stage.
statement: Exact hard-max polish after a softmax anneal adds negligible gain (<1e-5): p0040's hardpolish stage went 0.904958 -> 0.904962 (+0.000004).

why: p0042's coarsening ladder gained +0.000400, essentially equal to p0043's fixed-N reheat +0.000411; the claim that coarsening reaches better regions is not supported.
Direct measurement of a hop cycle gaining 3.3e-4.
statement: Large multiplicative basin-hopping (sigma U(0.05,0.20), optional zeroing of smallest 10-20%) followed by re-annealing escapes p0043's basin to a structurally different one: p0048 scored 0.907903 (+0.000334) with 40.8% zeros and f*f max at 0.303, versus p0043's 41.1% zeros / 0.302.

why: Two very different shapes with nearly equal R.
statement: At least two structurally different basins reach ~0.9079: p0047 (1.7% zeros, f*f max at 0.496) and p0048 (40.8% zeros, max at 0.303). R is largely insensitive to these structural details, so remaining gains come from hopping between basins and adding resolution, not from refining one basin's shape.
refuted_if: Local refinement of a single basin beats all cross-basin hops by more than 1e-3.

why: p0048 shows the escape route; p0047 confirms hard polish is negligible.
statement: The p0043 basin is saturated for small reheat (+4.1e-4 over 4 cycles, p0043; +3.9e-4 over 3 cycles, p0047), but large-sigma hops escape to a different basin at +3.3e-4 (p0048). Exact hard-R polish after softmax anneal adds <1e-5 (p0040 +4e-6, p0047 +6e-6). Remaining gains are ~1e-4-5e-4.

why: Another independent reheat run lands at the same ~4e-4 scale.
statement: Re-heating at fixed N is a cheap but saturating escape: p0043's 4 cycles at N=800 gained +4.1e-4, p0047's 3 cycles gained +3.9e-4 (0.907570->0.907962), p0042's ladder +4.0e-4. Gains are ~4e-4, not 1e-3.

why: Second independent confirmation.
statement: Exact hard-max polish after a softmax anneal adds negligible gain (<1e-5): p0040's hard stage +4e-6, p0047's hard stage 0.907962->0.907962 and final 0.907962->0.907968 (+6e-6).

why: p-norm adds another negative surrogate result; the T prescription is now the thing to test.
statement: Replacing the hard max with softmax_T (log-sum-exp, annealed T) gives dense gradients weighting all near-max knots and is the main lever found; re-heating T back to ~1e-3*maxL after annealing to 1e-6-1e-7*maxL escapes the local basin. Softmax beats top-k (0.789) and p-norm (0.904529, 0.000000 gain).
refuted_if: A reheat-temperature sweep at N=800 finds a T_hi outside [3e-4,3e-3]*maxL that gains >=1e-4 over p0047's best while the standard T_hi=1e-3 gains <1e-5, or softmax-smoothed ascent gains <1e-4 over 20+ s while perturb-restart cycles on the same base gain more.

why: Superseded by later dense-bump results; no new test needed.
Qualitative peaked-shape claim subsumed by B10/B16 and softmax mechanism.
Symmetry claim no longer informative at current ~0.908 level.
Resolution-alone belief tested and superseded by B13/B16.
Sparse comb claim parked pending reopened A6 test.
Detailed p0043 shape description is obsolete after p0052.
Flat-f*f claim not driving current hopping gains.
Already marked dropped.
Coarsening claim superseded by hop/reheat comparison.

refuted_if: Large-sigma hopping from p0047/p0052 at N=800-1600 gains <1e-5 while pure reheat from p0047 gains >=1e-4.
Local refinement of a single basin beats all cross-basin hops by more than 1e-3.
A pure reheat run from p0047 or p0052, with no large hops, reaches or exceeds 0.908417.
An 8+ cycle fixed-N reheat from p0052 gains more than 1e-3 without basin hopping.

text: Current best 0.908417 (p0052) is a large-sigma hop basin, about +4.5e-4 over p0047. Softmax/logsumexp analytic ascent remains the core lever; exact hard polish adds <1e-5. Fixed-N reheat saturates near +4e-4, while large multiplicative hops now give the best gains. At least three structurally different basins (p0047, p0048, p0052) score ~0.908, so R is relatively insensitive to zero gaps and f*f max location. Untested: N=1600 hopping/reheat from p0052, optimal T_hi for this basin, and whether sparse/comb shapes can challenge the dense bump. Constant function remains 2/3.

why: Hop is now the single best gain (+4.5e-4), confirming it as a distinct lever from reheat.
statement: Large multiplicative basin-hopping (sigma U(0.05,0.25), optional zeroing of the smallest 10-20%) followed by re-annealing escapes to structurally different basins: p0048 +3.3e-4 (40.8% zeros, f*f max 0.303), p0052 +4.5e-4 (5.4% zeros, max 0.373, best 0.908417).

why: Two more fixed-N reheat runs land in the same ~4e-4 band.
statement: Re-heating at fixed N is a cheap but saturating escape: p0043 +4.1e-4, p0047 +3.9e-4, p0055 +3.7e-4 (0.907968->0.908339), p0054 +1.4e-4. Gains are ~4e-4, not 1e-3.

why: Reinforces that per-basin gains are ~4e-4 and polish is negligible; the open question is whether a new perturbation geometry finds a new basin.
statement: The p0043/p0047 basin is saturated for small reheat (~4e-4), but large hops escape to new basins (p0048 +3.3e-4, p0052 +4.5e-4). p0052's hop gained all +4.5e-4 in cycle 1 and 0 in cycles 2-4; exact hard polish adds <1e-5 (p0052 +2e-6, p0055 +2e-6).

why: Two more confirmations; polish is not where gains come from.
statement: Exact hard-max polish after a softmax anneal adds negligible gain (<1e-5): p0040 +4e-6, p0047 +6e-6, p0052 +2e-6, p0055 +2e-6.

why: Four near-equal basins with very different structure; supports basin-finding over local refinement.
statement: At least three structurally different basins reach >=0.9079: p0047 (1.7% zeros, max 0.496), p0048 (40.8% zeros, max 0.303), p0052 (5.4% zeros, max 0.373); p0055 (4.5% zeros, max 0.671) may be a mirror-related basin. R is largely insensitive to zero-gap structure, so gains come from finding new basins, not refining one.

why: The T_hi challenge gained more than predicted overall but showed no attribution to a nonstandard T; the refuted_if condition was not met.
statement: Softmax_T (log-sum-exp, annealed T) gives dense gradients weighting all near-max knots and is the main lever; re-heating T to ~1e-3*maxL after annealing to 1e-6-1e-7*maxL escapes the local basin. T_hi=1e-3*maxL is near-optimal: the p0054 sweep gained +1.4e-4 with no evidence a T_hi outside [3e-4,3e-3] won, and p0055's standard-T reheat gained +3.7e-4.

why: Motivates changing perturbation geometry rather than adding more iid cycles.
statement: Hop gains come from a single lucky cycle; subsequent iid hops at the same sigma add ~0: p0052 cycle 1 +4.5e-4 (16.6 s), cycles 2-4 exactly 0.

why: p0058 directly tests N=1600 reheat on the p0052 hop basin and gains +1.06e-4.
statement: The p0052 hop basin is saturated at N=800 (iid hops add 0 after cycle 1), but mass-preserving upsample to N=1600 plus reheat adds +1.06e-4 (p0058); exact hard polish remains <1e-5.

why: p0058's N=1600 reheat gain is consistent with the ~1e-4 saturation scale.
statement: Re-heating at fixed N is a cheap but saturating escape: p0043 +4.1e-4, p0047 +3.9e-4, p0055 +3.7e-4, p0054 +1.4e-4, p0058 +1.06e-4 at N=1600.

why: Direct comparison of block-segment hopping against the iid hop that produced p0052.
statement: Block/segment perturbations are not a better escape than iid per-step hops: p0059 gained only +1.4e-5 at N=800 vs p0052's +4.5e-4.

why: p0060 tests the structural-move family and falls ~1.2e-3 short of the best.
statement: Structural moves on a dense bump (contiguous zero gap, added second hump) reach only 0.907274 (p0060), far below the dense single-bump best 0.908523; sparse/multi-hump structure is not competitive.

why: p0058 reproduces the one-lucky-cycle pattern at N=1600.
statement: Hop gains come from a single lucky cycle; subsequent iid hops at the same sigma add ~0: p0052 cycle 1 +4.5e-4, cycles 2-4 exactly 0; p0058 cycle 1 +1.05e-4, cycle 2 exactly 0.

why: p0066 confirms hop saturation at N=1600; p0065 shows the remaining reheat gains are small and structural (basin shift), not resolution.
statement: The p0052 hop basin is saturated for large-sigma hops at both N=800 (p0052 cycles 2-4 = 0) and N=1600 (p0066 = 0), but small-sigma reheat with upsampling still adds: +1.06e-4 at N=1600 (p0058) and +4.7e-5 more (p0065, which also shifted to a 39.8%-zero structure). Exact hard polish remains <1e-5.

why: p0065 continues the monotone decline of reheat gains; p0066 shows hop adds nothing at N=1600.
statement: Re-heating at fixed N is a cheap but saturating escape: p0043 +4.1e-4, p0047 +3.9e-4, p0055 +3.7e-4, p0054 +1.4e-4, p0058 +1.06e-4, p0065 +4.7e-5; large-sigma hop at N=1600 adds 0 (p0066).

why: p0066 is a direct N=1600 test of the hop mechanism and it gives zero.
statement: Large multiplicative basin-hopping (sigma U(0.05,0.25), optional zeroing) escapes to structurally different basins at N=800 (p0048 +3.3e-4, p0052 +4.5e-4), but at N=1600 the same large-sigma hop from p0058 adds exactly 0 (p0066): hop escape is resolution-dependent and saturates at N=1600.

why: p0065's statistics match p0048's zero-gap basin, suggesting the best line has moved into that family.
statement: At least four structurally different basins reach >=0.9079: p0047 (1.7% zeros, max 0.496), p0048 (40.8% zeros, max 0.303), p0052 (5.4% zeros, max 0.373), p0055 (4.5% zeros, max 0.671); p0065 (39.8% zeros, max 0.302, 0.908570) refines the p0048 zero-gap family and is now the best. R is largely insensitive to zero-gap structure; the zero-gap family may be marginally best.

why: p0066 is a third independent confirmation that repeat hops add nothing.
statement: Hop gains come from a single lucky cycle; subsequent iid hops at the same sigma add ~0: p0052 cycle 1 +4.5e-4, cycles 2-4 = 0; p0058 cycle 1 +1.05e-4, cycle 2 = 0; p0066 three cycles all 0.

why: p0063 tests the sparse family from scratch and lands far below the dense bump.
statement: Structural moves on a dense bump (contiguous zero gap, added second hump) reach only 0.907274 (p0060), and a from-scratch sparse comb (K=40 spikes, N=2000) with softmax anneal reaches only 0.868008 (p0063): sparse/multi-hump structure is not competitive with the dense bump.

why: p0065's hard stage added 0.000001.
statement: Exact hard-max polish after a softmax anneal adds negligible gain (<1e-5): p0040 +4e-6, p0047 +6e-6, p0052 +2e-6, p0055 +2e-6, p0065 +1e-6.

why: Trivial baseline (constant = 2/3) no longer informs any decision; keeping beliefs few.
Both a resolution reheat and a hot-temperature reheat returned 0.000000, confirming saturation.
statement: Fixed-N reheat is a saturating escape: p0043 +4.1e-4, p0047 +3.9e-4, p0055 +3.7e-4, p0054 +1.4e-4, p0058 +1.06e-4, p0065 +4.7e-5, and now p0069 (N=3200 reheat) and p0070 (hot T_hi 3e-3/1e-2) both add exactly 0. Reheat is exhausted; gains must come from hop geometry.

why: Forced N=3200 reheat from p0065 gave 0, while a fixed-N=1600 mixed hop gave +6.5e-5.
statement: The p0052/p0065 hop basin is saturated for pure reheat at N=1600 AND N=3200 (p0066=0, p0069=0). Resolution is not a lever past N=1600; further gains require changing the shape via hop, as p0073 did (+6.5e-5).

why: p0073's mixed perturbations and more cycles gained where pure large-sigma p0066 did not.
statement: Pure large-sigma hop saturates at N=1600 (p0066=0), but mixed-sigma hop (bands spanning small to large, more cycles, repeated hard polish) still escapes: p0073 +6.5e-5 over p0065 at fixed N=1600. Hop escape depends on the perturbation mix and cycle count, not just sigma magnitude.

why: Only recent gain at N=1600, and it came from the hop stage.
statement: p0073-style strong mixed basin-hopping at fixed N=1600 (mixed sigma bands, many cycles, repeated hard polish at multiple lrs) is the current best escape: +6.5e-5 over p0065 to 0.908635, with the gain appearing in the hop stage (hard polish added 0).

why: Blur-then-reheat from p0034 topped out at 0.9072.
statement: Gaussian blurring at multiple widths is a weak escape: p0071 gained +9e-5 but only reached 0.907249, far below the 0.9086 best.

why: Two consecutive generations of hop gains at fixed N=1600; hard polish still adds 0.
statement: Extended mixed basin-hopping at fixed N=1600 (multi-sigma multiplicative bands, optional zeroing/wobble, 5-6 stage anneals, repeated hard polish) is the current best escape: p0073 +6.5e-5 (0.908635), p0076 +7.6e-5 (0.908711), i.e. +1.4e-4 over p0065 across two generations.

why: p0076 again gains in the hop stage; p0079 shows the same code also improves a distant basin (+2.1e-4).
statement: Mixed-sigma hop escapes at fixed N=1600 where pure large-sigma hop and reheat saturate: p0073 +6.5e-5, p0076 +7.6e-5 over p0065/p0073. Escape depends on perturbation mix and cycle count, not resolution or temperature.

why: p0076 reproduces the one-lucky-cycle pattern exactly.

statement: At least six structurally different basins reach >=0.9073: p0047 (1.7% zeros, max 0.496), p0048 (40.8% zeros, max 0.303), p0052 (5.4% zeros, max 0.373), p0055 (max 0.671), p0065 (39.8% zeros), and now p0079 (7.6% zeros, f*f max at 0.963 of support, 0.907370). R is relatively insensitive to zero gaps and f*f max location.

statement: Hop is basin-dependent: the same strong mixed-hop code from the p0034 fork point (upsampled to N=1600) improves +2.1e-4 but only reaches 0.907370, ~1.3e-3 below the p0065/p0073/p0076 lineage. Hop improves any start but its reachable ceiling depends on the starting basin.

statement: Low-dimensional smooth parametric families are non-competitive: a 3-Gaussian mixture (9 params, Nelder-Mead multistart) plus softmax anneal reaches only 0.879002, far below 0.9087.

why: Gains have shrunk monotonically (4.5e-4 -> 1.06e-4 -> 6.5e-5 -> 7.6e-5) and every non-hop lever tested adds 0.
statement: With the current toolkit (softmax reheat + mixed multiplicative hop + hard polish) at fixed N<=3200 starting from the p0076 basin, R cannot exceed 0.9100; gains beyond 0.9087 require a structurally different construction (e.g. designed autoconvolution) or a new perturbation family.
refuted_if: Any reheat/hop run from p0076 (or an ancestor) at N<=3200 reaches R >= 0.9100.

Any reheat/hop run from p0076 or an ancestor at N<=3200 reaches R >= 0.9100.

text: Best 0.908711 (p0076), plateau ~2 gens. Softmax/hard polish is mature; fixed-N reheat and pure high-N are saturated. Mixed-sigma hop is the best escape but gains are rare one-cycle events and basin-dependent: p0076 +7.6e-5, p0085 lifts a smooth start only to 0.87995. Direct flat-top autoconvolution design (0.8608), low-dim Gaussian mixtures (0.8790), and sparse combs (0.8680) are noncompetitive. Current recipe is dense-bump basin plus strong hop; next test is targeted f*f-shaping perturbation rather than iid hop, and one sharper flat-top design. A ceiling near 0.9100 remains conjectural.

why: p0084 (wide hop, cheaper/more cycles from p0076) added exactly 0; p0085 (hop from smooth basin) gained once then stalled. Single-lucky-cycle saturation holds.
Cheaper/more-cycle wide mixed hop from p0076 also added 0, reinforcing saturation at 0.908711.
Hop from the smooth 3-Gaussian basin stalls at 0.87995, ~0.028 below the dense-bump best, supporting basin-dependence.
Designed flat-top (super-Gaussian target) reaches only 0.8608 with a peaked f*f, another low-dim/designed family failing.
Neither wide hop from p0076 nor hop from a smooth basin exceeds 0.908711/0.87995, consistent with the ~0.91 ceiling.
Direct measurement: designed target did not produce a flat f*f.
statement: Designed flat-top autoconvolution fails at the fit stage: p0083's target super-Gaussian plateau (p=8,w=0.7) yields f*f with inf 1.295 (peaked, not flat) and R=0.8608 — the inversion produces a peaked basin, so the flat-top region is not actually reached.

why: The 20-cycle small-sigma challenge produced exactly 0, confirming single-lucky-cycle behaviour.
statement: Hop gains come from a single lucky cycle; subsequent iid hops at the same or smaller sigma add ~0: p0052 cycle1 +4.5e-4 then 0; p0058 +1.05e-4 then 0; p0066 0,0,0; p0076 cycle1 +7.6e-5, cycle2 = 0; p0084 (cheaper, more cycles) 0; p0090 (20 small-sigma cycles) 0.

why: Three further hop variants from the same basin give zero.
statement: Extended mixed basin-hopping at fixed N=1600 was the best escape (p0073 +6.5e-5, p0076 +7.6e-5) but is now saturated: p0084 (cheaper/more cycles + additive bumps), p0089 (targeted f*f-shape field) and p0090 (many small-sigma cycles) all add exactly 0 at 0.908711.

why: The sharper target and direct R-optimization both failed to flatten f*f.
statement: Designed flat-top autoconvolution fails at both the fit and the refinement stage: p0083 (p=8,w=0.7) gives a peaked f*f (inf 1.295) at R=0.8608, and p0091 (p=2,w=0.9 target + long direct softmax anneal from p0083's f) stays at 0.860762 with f*f still peaked.

why: Every perturbation family tested adds exactly 0 from p0076.
statement: With the current toolkit (softmax reheat + mixed multiplicative hop + targeted f*f-shape perturbation + hard polish) at fixed N<=3200 from the p0076 basin, R is capped near 0.90875; gains beyond require a different optimizer geometry or a structurally different construction.

why: Hop lever is exhausted at this basin.
statement: Mixed-sigma hop escaped at fixed N=1600 where pure large-sigma hop and reheat saturated (p0073, p0076), but is itself now saturated at 0.908711 (p0084, p0090 = 0). Escape depends on perturbation mix and cycle count, not resolution or temperature.

why: Three independent perturbation families all return exactly the start's score.
statement: p0076 is a strict local optimum under all tested multiplicative/zeroing perturbation families: wide iid mixed hop (p0084, 0), targeted low-frequency field from the f*f near-max shape (p0089, 0), and 20 small-sigma cycles (p0090, 0).
refuted_if: a construction that does better than this statement says is possible

why: Explains why the deterministic shaping sweep gave exactly 0 while iid hop once gave +7.6e-5.
statement: Targeted perturbations built from the smoothed R-gradient / anti-max field of f*f are locally equivalent to a softmax reheat: they perturb along the same near-max-knot direction PGD already follows, so they cannot leave the basin. Escapes need a direction orthogonal to the near-max-knot subspace or a different optimizer path.
refuted_if: A targeted perturbation with amplitude alpha>=0.3 or a field built from a different functional of L (e.g. edge/second-moment weighting) gains >1e-5 from p0076.

why: Hard polish is negligible and mature; no longer decision-relevant.
Structural/sparse-comb non-competitiveness is subsumed by B24 and the flat-top failures.
p0097 overturns the earlier view that smooth starts are inferior; they reach a higher basin.
statement: Hop is basin-dependent and the smooth 3-Gaussian basin is a SUPERIOR seed: hop from it reaches 0.909367 (p0097), ABOVE the dense-bump p0076 (0.908711); hop from the p0034 fork point reached only 0.907370 (p0079). The reachable ceiling depends strongly on start structure, and smooth starts beat dense bumps.

why: Direct parametric is weak but as a starting basin it is the new best.
statement: Low-dimensional smooth parametric families are weak as direct constructions (3-Gaussian reaches only 0.879002, p0078/p0085) but are EXCELLENT hop seeds: hopped from the smooth basin they reach 0.909367 (p0097).

why: p0097 exceeds the previously conjectured cap; the cap applies only to the p0076 basin.
statement: With the current toolkit at fixed N<=3200, the p0076 dense-bump basin is capped near 0.90875 (p0096 CD=0), but the smooth-start basin exceeds this at 0.909367 (p0097). The cap is basin-specific, not global.

why: CD also adds exactly 0 at p0076, closing the last local-search geometry.
statement: p0076 is a strict local optimum under all tested escapes: wide iid hop (p0084=0), targeted f*f-shaping (p0089=0), 20 small-sigma cycles (p0090=0), and exact coordinate descent (p0096=0). Escape required a different START, not a different perturbation.

why: Fixed-N reheat saturation is superseded; the live lever is now start-basin choice, not reheat.
Flat-top design failure is settled and no longer central to the search.
This is the biggest gain of the run and redefines the best line.
statement: A smooth 3-Gaussian start (p0085, 0.879951), mass-preserving upsampled to N=1600 and run through mixed-sigma hop + exact coordinate descent + reheat, reaches 0.909367 (p0097) — a new best basin above the dense-bump p0076 (0.908711); the hop was still climbing at cycle 4 (0.906480 -> 0.908822 -> 0.909093).

why: Explains why a new start, not a new perturbation, was the escape.
statement: The smooth-start basin (p0097) has a different f*f geometry (max at 0.644 of support, 46.9% of knots within 5% of max) than the dense-bump basin (max at 0.423), and is less saturated by hop: it gained across 4 cycles where the dense-bump basin was dead. Hop saturation is basin-specific, not global.
refuted_if: More hop cycles from p0097 at N=1600 add 0 while the same schedule from a fresh smooth seed gains >=1e-4.

statement: With the current toolkit at fixed N<=3200, the p0076 dense-bump basin is capped near 0.90875, and the smooth-start basin (p0097, 0.909367) is itself capped under extended mixed hop + CD + reheat at N=1600 (p0102 = 0 across 5 cycles). Caps are basin-specific AND optimizer-specific, not global.
refuted_if: Any reheat/hop/CD run from p0076 or p0097 at N<=3200 reaches R >= 0.9100.

why: p0102 is the saturation test for the p0097 basin.
statement: A smooth 3-Gaussian start (p0085, 0.879951), mass-preserving upsampled to N=1600 and run through mixed-sigma hop + exact coordinate descent + reheat, reaches 0.909367 (p0097) — the best basin found. It saturates there: 5 further hop cycles, CD and reheat add exactly 0 (p0102).

why: p0102 extends the pattern to the new best basin.
statement: Hop gains come from a single lucky cycle; subsequent iid hops at the same or smaller sigma add ~0: p0052 cycle1 +4.5e-4 then 0; p0058 +1.05e-4 then 0; p0066 0,0,0; p0076 cycle1 +7.6e-5, cycle2 = 0; p0084 0; p0090 0; p0097 gained across 4 cycles but then 5 more cycles added exactly 0 (p0102).

The smooth-start basin (p0097) has a different f*f geometry (max at 0.644-0.684 of support, ~47% of knots within 5% of max) than the dense-bump basin (max at 0.423). Its hop gains came early (4 cycles) and are now exhausted: more hop cycles at N=1600 add 0 (p0102).
refuted_if: More hop cycles from p0097 at N=1600 add >=1e-5 while the same schedule from a fresh smooth seed gains >=1e-4.

why: p0099 is the from-scratch smooth-seed test.
statement: Low-dimensional smooth parametric families are weak as direct constructions (3-Gaussian 0.879002, p0078/p0085) but are good hop seeds: hopped from the smooth basin they reach 0.909367 (p0097). From-scratch smooth seeds with the full hop+CD recipe reach only 0.887136 (p0099), so the WARM start matters, not just the seed family.

why: Superseded by B27 (p0076 strict local optimum) and B25 (basin-specific caps); keeping both duplicates evidence.
Direct saturation measurement on the best basin.
statement: The p0097 smooth-start basin is a strict local optimum under the current toolkit: extended mixed hop (5 cycles, p0102 = 0), exact coordinate descent (p0102 coord stage = 0) and reheat (p0102 reheat stage = 0) all add exactly 0 at 0.909367. Further gains need a different optimizer geometry or a different seed.
refuted_if: a construction that does better than this statement says is possible

why: Refuted: p0107 reached 0.912988 from the p0097 line, above the conjectured ~0.9100 cap.
Refuted: the p0097 basin was NOT a local optimum — L-BFGS added +0.0036 (p0107).
Geometry description of a basin that is no longer saturated; superseded by the optimizer finding.
Low value now that the escape came from optimizer geometry, not perturbation direction.
Hop-cycle accounting is superseded: L-BFGS, not hop, is now the live lever.
Same surrogate, same basin, different optimizer → +0.0036.
statement: Hard-max local ascent saturates ~0.844; smoothed-max ascent with exact gradients is the dominant lever, and the optimizer matters as much as the smoothing: Adam PGD on softmax saturates at 0.909367 while annealed L-BFGS-B on the same surrogate reaches 0.912988 (p0107, +0.0036).

why: p0107 annealed the same T ladder through L-BFGS and gained +0.0036.
statement: Softmax_T (log-sum-exp, annealed T from 1e-3 to 1e-8*maxL) gives dense near-max-knot gradients and is the main smoothing lever; with L-BFGS-B as the inner solver it is much stronger than with Adam PGD, and re-heating to ~1e-3*maxL still escapes local basins.

why: p0108 is the new from-scratch record.
statement: Low-dimensional smooth parametric families are weak as direct constructions (3-Gaussian 0.8790) but are good seeds: hopped they reach 0.909367 (p0097), and from-scratch smooth seeds with the full hop+CD+reheat recipe reach 0.894767 (p0108) — still ~0.018 below the warm-start best.

why: Pairwise transfer, the last untested move family, added exactly 0.
statement: p0076 is a strict local optimum under every tested escape: wide iid hop, targeted f*f-shaping, 20 small-sigma cycles, exact coordinate descent, and pairwise mass-transfer line search (p0106 = 0 across 4 sweeps). Escape required a different START, not a different perturbation.

why: The 'saturation' was optimizer-specific.
statement: A smooth 3-Gaussian start (p0085) upsampled and run through mixed-sigma hop + CD + reheat reaches 0.909367 (p0097); it is saturated for Adam PGD/hop/CD but NOT for L-BFGS-B, which lifts it to 0.912988 (p0107).

why: Single largest gain in 3 generations, from a basin declared saturated.
statement: Annealed L-BFGS-B on the softmax surrogate (analytic gradient, h>=0 bounds, T ladder 1e-3→1e-8*maxL, N=400→800 continuation, CD between stages) is a far stronger local optimizer than Adam PGD: from the Adam-saturated p0102 (0.909367) it gains +0.003621 to 0.912988 in 2.85 s.

why: 90% of the budget was unused when the big gain landed.
statement: The p0107 recipe's gains are budget-limited, not basin-limited: it stopped at 2.85 s of 30 s, so at fixed N the same annealed L-BFGS continuation run to ~95% of budget (more T stages, warm restarts, CD sweeps, N=1600 continuation) should keep adding real gains.
refuted_if: A full-budget (>=25 s CPU) annealed L-BFGS run from p0107 at N=800 or N=1600 adds <1e-5.

why: Extrapolating from a 2.85 s run that gained 3.6e-3.
statement: The p0107 basin (0.912988) is not saturated: full-budget annealed L-BFGS with N=800→1600 continuation reaches R >= 0.915.
refuted_if: Full-budget L-BFGS runs from p0107 at N=800 and N=1600 both add <1e-5.

why: p0108 is the from-scratch record and shows headroom remains.
statement: From-scratch smooth seeds plus the full hop+CD+reheat recipe reach 0.894767 (p0108), a +0.0076 gain over p0099's 0.887136, but still ~0.018 below the warm-start best; the from-scratch line is viable but needs the new L-BFGS engine.

text: The problem is dominated by the local optimizer, not by a low global ceiling: annealed L-BFGS-B on the softmax surrogate lifted the smooth-start basin from 0.909367 to 0.929570 (p0112), with p0114 at 0.925130. Earlier 0.908-0.910 ceilings were optimizer/budget limits. Fixed-N reheat/hop and pairwise/CD moves are locally saturated but not globally informative. The current best is a smooth-seeded, highly asymmetric dense-ish profile with broad near-max f*f support. From-scratch recipes remain ~0.018 lower (p0108), so seed structure still matters. Next: full-budget L-BFGS continuation at higher N, re-base power-mean on p0112, test basin specificity, and retry from-scratch with L-BFGS.

why: Three independent full-budget runs all gained, and the wrapper (perturb-restart cycles) beat the plain anneal.
statement: Annealed L-BFGS-B on the softmax surrogate is the strongest local optimizer found: +0.0036 from p0102 (p0107), +0.0121 from p0107 at full budget (p0114, 0.925130), and the p0112 perturb-restart wrapper adds a further +0.0044 at N=1600 (0.929570).

why: Both full-budget runs kept gaining where the short runs had stopped.
statement: Gains are budget-limited, not basin-limited: p0114's full-budget run added +0.0121 over p0107's 2.85 s run, and p0112's 7 perturb-restart cycles added +4.4e-4 in 19.5 s after the L-BFGS stages — still positive at the end.

why: Two different from-scratch recipes both stay far below 0.93.
statement: From-scratch smooth seeds with hop+CD reach 0.894767 (p0108) and with the L-BFGS engine only 0.889109 (p0115), still ~0.035-0.04 below the warm-start best; the warm smooth-start basin is essential so far.

why: Per second of CPU the power-mean engine is far stronger and follows a different ascent path.
statement: The power-mean (p-norm) surrogate annealed in q is a competitive, much cheaper alternative: p0113 reached 0.923883 in 5.2 s (83% of budget unused) vs softmax's 0.925130 in 23.8 s (p0114), and it lands in a different f*f geometry (max at 0.732 vs 0.781/0.956).

why: p0113 and p0114 reach similar scores but visibly different f*f shapes, so the two surrogates explore different regions.
statement: Alternating power-mean (cheap exploration) and softmax (sharp polish) surrogates inside the perturb-restart loop should beat either alone on p0112, because they follow different ascent paths.
refuted_if: An alternating-surrogate full-budget run from p0112 at N=1600 adds <1e-5 over 0.929570.

why: Every time the optimizer or budget improved, the 'ceiling' moved up by >0.01.
statement: The true maximum of R is above 0.94; the ~0.93 level is an optimizer/budget artifact, not a ceiling.
refuted_if: Five independent full-budget runs (different seeds, surrogates, resolutions) all stay below 0.935.
